page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a cloud server configuration within the High Performance family, utilizing an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The instance is allocated 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores via hyperthreading, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 and AES instructions. The hardware envelope integrates 12 GB of system RAM, providing 3.0 GB of memory per vCPU, alongside 260 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Discrete GPU acceleration is not present.

Performance assessments display moderate single-core capabilities contrasted with lower multi-core scaling. The processor achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1,165 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1,466.08, situating it within median industry percentiles. Multi-core execution ranks in lower tiers due to the two physical core constraint and shared resource allocation, registering 3,734 on Geekbench multi-core and 17.19 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In-memory execution reveals high cached bandwidth at 421.33 GB/sec, dropping to 36.96 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads, while Redis SET throughput reaches 6.4 million operations per second.

The qualitative cost profile favors setups requiring significant local storage capacity and moderate memory without demanding dedicated high-throughput multi-core compute. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on shared vCPU contention during sustained parallel processing. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for web serving, staging environments, Redis caching layers, continuous integration workers, and light database operations requiring low-latency NVMe disk access.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a shared-core High Performance virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The server configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 12 GB of RAM (3.0 GB per core), and a bundled 260 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPUs. Hardware support includes 16 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 extensions. Synthetic benchmarks reveal mid-tier single-core execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,165 and Redis throughput of 6.4 million operations per second, though multi-threaded throughput and uncached memory access are constrained by the physical core count and shared compute model. Delivering high storage density relative to its resource footprint, this server is suitable for development environments, web hosting, intermediate caching nodes, and light database deployments.
